Lessons.Title: Find Angle Measurements
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will find unknown angle measurements by composing or decomposing known measurements, and to see that an angle is not determined by the length of the segments that form it.
In this lesson, you use tactile tools to find angle measurements and observe more clearly that angles are additive. You compose and decompose angles by arranging paper cutouts, by folding paper or tracing, and by drawing diagrams. You arrange smaller angles whose sizes are unknown into larger angles with familiar sizes and features ( \(90^\circ\) , \(180^\circ\) , and \(360^\circ\) ).

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Corner Pieces (10 minutes); Activity 1: How Big Are These Angles? (25 minutes); Activity 2: Angles in a Kite (10 minutes); Cool-down: Sets of Three Angles (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Adjacent angles compose a larger angle; subtract known parts from 90°, 180°, or a known total to find an unknown.

Edulytics authored guidance: Identify the right angle of 90° and its labelled part of 62°. Calculate the missing part: 90° − 62° = 28°. Explain that enlarging the segment drawings does not change their angle measurements.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): A straight angle contains a 73° part. What is the other adjacent angle?
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
